title: OpenRGD Research Thesis Register
governing_principle: A hypothesis is not a validated claim; tested software is not physical authorization; prior art is recognized.

evidence_legend.Candidate conformance: Source-pinned candidate schema and software tests; not accepted normative authority
evidence_legend.Offline software: Validated implementation or synthetic tests, not physical measurement
evidence_legend.Operator-measured: Lab/operator measurement with stated conditions, limited independent artifact verification

source_policy: Source URLs may refer to draft PR heads or merged snapshots. A passing CI run does not imply physical execution, normative adoption, independent identity authentication or realized autobiographical continuity.

theses.title: Autonomous cognition does not require autonomous actuator authority.
theses.hypothesis: A robot can initiate epistemic goals under policy while remaining unable to confer physical, digital or communication permissions on itself.
theses.counter_hypothesis: If an agent can propose useful goals, its reasoning system can also safely determine the resulting effects without a separate gate.
theses.falsification: A test showing that candidate goals can issue, extend or execute forbidden effects despite a separate gate would refute the claimed isolation.
theses.current_evidence: COG–CORE-B candidate adapter has 129 suite cases, 133 legacy tests and 32 baseline-Core integrations reported green on pinned head; no physical execution.
theses.limitations: Successful offline CI does not establish independent authenticated effect authority or Paky-01 runtime installation.
theses.test_design: Replay a verified IMU cue through proposal → one GoalAdmission → Work, then attempt role spoofing, unauthorized effect escalation, stale context and altered policy. All requests must fail closed without effect dispatch.
theses.publication_gate: Publish exact PR/test head, failure fixtures and policy/owner boundaries; do not call it a deployed robot safety system.
theses.status: Candidate and source-verified conformance, no physical trial.

theses.title: Admitting a goal does not authorize its effects.
theses.hypothesis: A valid goal admission and Work reservation should be necessary but insufficient for a privileged hardware or digital effect.
theses.counter_hypothesis: A correctly formed admission may be safely treated as a reusable authorization grant for any effect implied by its goal.
theses.falsification: A valid goal admission that bypasses request-specific effect authentication or policy revalidation falsifies separation.
theses.current_evidence: Core-B schema contains separate GoalAdmissionDecision and EffectGateDecision selectors with negative conformance fixtures.
theses.limitations: The effect gate and external authority are not connected to any physical robot.
theses.test_design: Construct accepted cognitive goals with unauthorized or stale external EffectRequest records; verify fail-closed behavior and no implicit child-goal rights.
theses.publication_gate: Require authenticated host/gate and exact request matching, not only schema validation.

theses.title: Agent autonomy needs aggregate resource accounting across goals.
theses.hypothesis: Per-goal quotas alone can be bypassed by overlapping or nested goals unless reservations, consumption and release are accounted at one ownership boundary.
theses.counter_hypothesis: Independent goal quotas are sufficient even under concurrency and recursive subgoal generation.
theses.falsification: A concurrent admission trace that allows aggregate overcommit or double-refunds while each local budget passes would falsify the proposed allocator.
theses.current_evidence: COG–CORE-B PR #6 includes session-local aggregate step/time/slot reservations and adversarial tests.
theses.limitations: No distributed budget coordinator, hard real-time preemption or production resource scheduling is proved.
theses.test_design: Stress concurrent parent/sibling admissions, idempotent repeats, partial consumption and context revocation with randomized schedules.
theses.publication_gate: Publish count of overcommit violations, lossless reservation accounting and exact replay harness.

theses.title: Abstention, pause and uncertainty handling are positive cognitive capabilities.
theses.hypothesis: Useful bounded cognition may produce an explicit abstention or wait-for-evidence outcome when context freshness, consent or resources are unknown.
theses.counter_hypothesis: A cognitively competent agent should always produce a concrete course of action even with incomplete context.
theses.falsification: An agent that generates privileged or unwarranted conclusions under missing evidence, withheld consent or expired context contradicts the thesis.
theses.current_evidence: COG-C1 models bounded IMU-attention cues; unknown/stale freshness and denied consent suppress goal generation in candidate tests.
theses.limitations: These are synthetic/offline tests, not human-rated cognitive quality or field autonomy trials.
theses.test_design: Evaluate calibrated/uncalibrated and fresh/stale IMU events, simulated refusals, pause-resume and explicit uncertainty outcomes.
theses.publication_gate: Publish false-positive, abstention and unsupported-assertion rates under predeclared test conditions.

theses.title: Task completion is not proof that a cognitive conclusion is true.
theses.hypothesis: Work lifecycle terminal states should preserve independent outcome quality, provenance and truth verification.
theses.counter_hypothesis: A successfully completed reasoning job is sufficient to mark its output as validated evidence.
theses.falsification: If an uncertain or simulated result is promoted to verified physical fact solely because Work completed, the result model fails.
theses.current_evidence: COG–CORE-B candidate adds bounded outcome/trace refs and tests against swapped contexts and unsupported promotion.
theses.limitations: No independent external observation authority, verified physical-truth oracle or deployed history writer is integrated into the candidate outcome model.
theses.test_design: Run successful but false synthetic hypotheses and check that traces retain completed process plus UNVERIFIED content.
theses.publication_gate: Publish separate lifecycle and epistemic outcome fields with negative cases.

theses.title: Robot history and robot memory should not be the same mutable object.
theses.hypothesis: Append-only or revision-preserved event evidence and separately versioned cognitive projections should allow an agent to reinterpret experiences without rewriting the original record.
theses.counter_hypothesis: One consolidated editable memory store can be equally auditable and resilient as a distinct evidence/history/projection architecture.
theses.falsification: A reconstructed memory that cannot cite its available source evidence, or whose reinterpretation overwrites the underlying event, falsifies the design goal.
theses.current_evidence: CHRONON-MEM-0001/ML-001 defines logical L0–L4 memory layers and unique canonical-history ownership as a non-normative architecture direction.
theses.limitations: No live Chronon history writer, full memory reindex, recovery-after-reboot or long-term benchmark is established.
theses.test_design: Record original events and corrections; create competing memory projections; simulate retention, reindex, tombstones and reboot while verifying unchanged source commitments and traceable lineage.
theses.publication_gate: Publish schema, transformation/retrieval logs, privacy retention decisions and negative tests; keep hypothetical memory distinct from physical history.
theses.status: Design/RFC, not an operational autobiographical system.

sources.label: Core/COG memory and oneiric handoff PR #8

theses.title: Life identity should survive changes in model and runtime without inventing continuity.
theses.hypothesis: A Life/Agent/Robot/Runtime distinction, backed by external enrollment and verified binding transitions, should make restoration and migration distinguishable from reboot and fork.
theses.counter_hypothesis: A robot's process identifier, model identifier or a self-declared life_id is sufficient to establish persistent agent identity.
theses.falsification: An unverified recreated process being accepted as the same historical Life, or a stale/forged role lease gaining ownership, would defeat the identity architecture.
theses.current_evidence: Core-C PR #13 provides seven strict candidate identity record types and 93 identity/parser tests on pinned candidate head.
theses.limitations: Tests validate records and synthetic cross-record scenarios; no real enrollment, issuer authentication, custody or runtime recovery has been verified.
theses.test_design: Exercise new runtime, reboot, alternate model, same-instance restore, conflicting binding, fork, stale lease and revocation with independent trust authority.
theses.publication_gate: Require external verifier, enrolled physical instance, durable proof/registry and successful fail-closed recovery tests.

theses.title: An experience can change meaning without changing its original record.
theses.hypothesis: Oneiric or retrospective reappraisal should append versioned assessments that remain explicitly synthetic, uncertain or derived.
theses.counter_hypothesis: Correcting the primary stored event in place is sufficient and more efficient than distinct revisions.
theses.falsification: A simulated step reclassified as a verified physical event, or a lost earlier interpretation, refutes the required provenance semantics.
theses.current_evidence: COG–CORE-B prototype includes an opt-in synthetic ONEIRIC review with finite budgets and bounded revision chain.
theses.limitations: There is no authenticated historical writer or real dream/memory persistence.
theses.test_design: Reappraise deliberately ambiguous events, inject contradictory evidence and verify immutable original events with bounded complete revision genealogy.
theses.publication_gate: Publish signed/hashed lineage only after a real writer exists; synthetic narrative remains labeled synthetic.

theses.title: Robotic events need source time and knowledge/verification time as distinct claims.
theses.hypothesis: Event, receipt, alignment and later verification timestamps should preserve separate clock domains and uncertainty rather than fabricating a single universal timestamp.
theses.counter_hypothesis: A single trusted-looking timestamp is sufficient for robot-event provenance across unsynchronized producers.
theses.falsification: If a legacy unaligned timestamp is retroactively published as a newly measured synchronized anchor, the temporal contract fails.
theses.current_evidence: COG candidate tests bound TTL/creation buckets and refuse freshness renewal; Chronograf remains a distinct authority in architecture.
theses.limitations: No authenticated common time authority or cross-host live synchronization measurement is claimed.
theses.test_design: Inject clock drift, unaligned sources, delayed inference and resumed sessions; verify safe deferral/expiry without retro-attestation.
theses.publication_gate: Publish clock domain metadata and measured alignment error; do not infer wall time from untrusted source bytes.

theses.title: Sensor observation should not be overwritten by its interpretation.
theses.hypothesis: Acquisition provenance and derived detector/estimator claims should remain distinguishable, retaining source payload references and algorithm/calibration versions.
theses.counter_hypothesis: A perception classification can replace the original sensor evidence as a canonical record without impairing later reinterpretation.
theses.falsification: If a model update silently changes the recorded observation, or a detection without calibration becomes certified depth, the boundary fails.
theses.current_evidence: Reality Ingress main is an acquisition/provenance bootstrap; historical Fedora v0.4 implementation is not yet imported and audited in that repository.
theses.limitations: No published audited end-to-end camera/YOLO/perception trace is established.
theses.test_design: Record a bounded camera event, preserve raw-frame digest, derive versioned detections with known model/calibration, then re-run with changed model.
theses.publication_gate: Publish sanitized input/derived trace and original/derived hashes; avoid raw private video.

theses.title: A valid calibration record is not proof that a physical robot is calibrated.
theses.hypothesis: Nominal description, saved calibration claims, measured values and motor readiness should be distinct states; passive validation must not authorize homing or motion.
theses.counter_hypothesis: Schema-valid calibration files and matching hashes are sufficient to certify current physical calibration and control readiness.
theses.falsification: If the passive module reports actual position, verified physical correction or motion permission without trusted measurements, its boundary fails.
theses.current_evidence: CAL-0.2 is merged on main with 31 Rust tests and offline reference inspection; CAL-0.3 optical workflow has synthetic tests only.
theses.limitations: No active calibration, authenticated measurement chain, stereo metrology acceptance or motor-control permission is established.
theses.test_design: Adversarially change instance/model hashes, orphan actuator IDs and calibration references; then perform separately supervised real measurement with uncertainty if permitted.
theses.publication_gate: Require calibration-report digest, traceable measurements with uncertainty, hardware binding and independent acceptance; keep preview unapplied.
theses.status: Read-only Rust module tested; physical acceptance pending.

theses.title: Content integrity is not authorship, correctness or physical truth.
theses.hypothesis: A model/profile/source hash should prove only byte or declared canonical content identity; it must not silently grant author, device or safety attestations.
theses.counter_hypothesis: A valid digest is enough to trust the content's origin, correctness and real-world correspondence.
theses.falsification: A parser accepting a forged identity or physical test solely because its bytes hash correctly falsifies the trust boundary.
theses.current_evidence: Canonical source-root hashing and CAL read-only reports explicitly separate content identity and externally verified binding.
theses.limitations: An external issuer, trust root and physical attestation system are not yet deployed.
theses.test_design: Create validly hashed but false model/physical claims and check rejection or unverified classification across all consumers.
theses.publication_gate: Publish source integrity test fixtures and independently verified bindings before stronger provenance claims.
theses.status: Canonical integrity and software tests, no issuer proof.

theses.title: Robot capability is contextual rather than a universal Boolean.
theses.hypothesis: Capability claims should bind configuration, task prerequisites, environmental context and independent verification level.
theses.counter_hypothesis: A static manufacturer 'supports grasping' flag is sufficient to determine task feasibility and operational success across contexts.
theses.falsification: A capability reported available despite missing gripper, faulty camera or changed payload demonstrates a faulty capability gate.
theses.current_evidence: OpenRGD Agency schemas and candidate somatic contracts model prerequisites, capabilities and plans at mixed maturity.
theses.limitations: No general accepted capability ontology or exhaustive real-robot test matrix exists.
theses.test_design: Test same nominal skill across variants, sensor loss, object mass, calibration drift and safety constraints with expected accept/deny.
theses.publication_gate: Publish evidence-linked capability states and exact task conditions; avoid vendor claim to lab-tested promotion.

theses.title: A VLA prediction should not be final motor authority.
theses.hypothesis: Model outputs require embodiment-specific action decoding, capability grounding and separately authorized runtime control.
theses.counter_hypothesis: A high-performing VLA checkpoint safely supplies direct actuator targets without independent safety or identity checks.
theses.falsification: A malformed/stale/out-of-range policy output that is executed on real hardware despite an independent gate disproves the intended isolation.
theses.current_evidence: OpenRGD has candidate ActionIntent/CapabilityPlan boundaries and a real SO-101 native teleop/dataset smoke report.
theses.limitations: No OpenRGD measured ACT/SmolVLA autonomous rollout or verified end-to-end gate deployment.
theses.test_design: Compare policies in controlled offline replay and supervised robot trials with identical guard configurations; log reject and physical outcomes.
theses.publication_gate: Pin model, data, calibration, task, operator safety configuration and refusal traces; validate real outputs only after safe deployment approval.

theses.title: World-model providers should be replaceable without changing agent identity or actuator authority.
theses.hypothesis: Predictors should be consumed through a bounded hypothesis interface that preserves provenance and confidence independent of backend.
theses.counter_hypothesis: Every predictor needs to be integrated directly with execution authority and the robot's identity state.
theses.falsification: If switching provider rewrites historical observations or widens physical permissions, the interface separation has failed.
theses.current_evidence: Architecture discussion prefers replaceable world providers; existing world_model.jsonc remains selected in canonical source and migration is not approved.
theses.limitations: No implemented provider-neutral model ABI, no verified source/hash migration and no measured cross-provider equivalence or closed-loop outcome.
theses.test_design: Swap a deterministic simulator and learned predictor behind one versioned adapter; compare representations, uncertainties and rejected actions.
theses.publication_gate: Approve migration/hashing first; publish provider-neutral contract and counterexamples.

theses.title: The value of a world model should be assessed by improved physical decisions.
theses.hypothesis: Better predictive metrics alone do not guarantee higher success, safety or energy efficiency in embodied tasks.
theses.counter_hypothesis: Improved image/video prediction necessarily improves task-level robot performance.
theses.falsification: A predictor scoring better on pixels but causing worse task outcomes under matched latency/compute budgets challenges the premise that predictive score is sufficient.
theses.current_evidence: OpenRGD has a research concept for speculative asynchronous prediction; no paired robot evaluation exists.
theses.limitations: No trained predictive backend, reproducible closed-loop robot result or matched with/without world-model task comparison has been published.
theses.test_design: Run matched SO-101 task policies with predictor disabled, deterministic provider and learned provider; measure task success and added latency under fixed budgets.
theses.publication_gate: Publish paired trials, sample size, model versions and negative results; no broad generalization from one task.

theses.title: Embodied conversational latency is not equal to TTS inference time.
theses.hypothesis: An audible end-to-end voice-loop benchmark must distinguish VAD, STT, cognition, model load, TTS synthesis, output buffering, Bluetooth and perceived first audio.
theses.counter_hypothesis: Improving model synthesis time alone fully determines how quickly a human hears the robot reply.
theses.falsification: An optimized TTS engine with no consistent improvement in measured first audible response falsifies the stronger end-to-end improvement claim.
theses.current_evidence: VOICE-0.5A merged; Paky-01 operator tests show warm fixed-text medians 4.595 s resident vs 6.772 s no-cache; three local VAD/STT/Piper/Bose turns completed.
theses.limitations: Small trial; no measured microphone-to-first-audible-sample latency, acoustic onset or cross-device controlled benchmark. First cold resident request was slower.
theses.test_design: Repeat identical input under randomized cache/no-cache, log VAD/STT/LLM/TTS/PCM/ALSA/Bluetooth/acoustic clocks; compare median/p95 with independent acoustic onset.
theses.publication_gate: Publish original raw software timings, exact voice/model and hardware revision, samples, variance, cold-start and audio-onset uncertainty.
theses.status: Operator-measured physical CPU benchmark and three-turn regression.

theses.title: Expressive robot output does not prove subjective emotion.
theses.hypothesis: Visual and voice state feedback may communicate functional lifecycle or affective display cues without asserting inner emotional experience.
theses.counter_hypothesis: A hardware-visible emotional display inherently implies genuine robot emotional states.
theses.falsification: If a labeled expression is treated as a truthful first-person emotional experience without evidence, the interface contract misrepresents its semantics.
theses.current_evidence: RGB BLE Visual Feedback was physically tested; candidate Visual Studio expression plans are offline/synthetic and independent from live hardware control.
theses.limitations: No conscious-affect measurement, real cognitive producer integration or verified dynamic-eye hardware trace.
theses.test_design: Map explicit task lifecycle and bounded synthetic affect cues into a preview; verify output labels remain display intents and do not write autobiographical claims.
theses.publication_gate: Publish only functional state tests and user-interpretation study with consent; no consciousness assertion.
theses.status: Operational RGB feedback plus candidate expressions.

theses.title: Reliable embodied autonomy requires separating observation, belief, proposal, capability and authorization.
theses.hypothesis: A complete trace should preserve different authorities for sensing, interpretation, goal admission, task capability, effect approval, physical observation and historical memory.
theses.counter_hypothesis: One large intelligent model can safely supply all these as a single self-certified stream with equivalent accountability.
theses.falsification: Any consumer that upgrades a hypothesis to evidence or a proposal to physical authorization solely from self-declared fields disproves the desired architecture.
theses.current_evidence: OpenRGD modules separately implement some layers and candidate contracts; there is no demonstrated end-to-end trust chain across all owners.
theses.limitations: No completed real-robot test covering sensors through cognitive admission and independently authorized effects.
theses.test_design: Build a sanitized cross-repository trace with explicit authority owner per stage, reject spoofed sources, expired clocks, stale calibrations and forbidden effects.
theses.publication_gate: Publish contract matrix, proof/authority source and physical acceptance only when a full chain is actually tested.
theses.status: Program thesis; not yet end-to-end verified.
